result.summary: Adds an optional boolean option `sat_vb` to `getmempoolinfo`, `getnetworkinfo`, `estimatesmartfee`, and `estimaterawfee`, allowing callers to receive feerates formatted in sat/vB rather than BTC/kvB. Introduces `ValueFromFeeRate` in `core_io` to format feerates to three decimal places without integer truncation, avoiding rounding artifacts in sub-1 sat/vB environments.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core RPCs historically output feerates exclusively in BTC/kvB, whereas user tooling and the wider ecosystem use sat/vB. Downstream clients must manually convert these units, adding client-side complexity and risking rounding errors or integer truncation in sub-1 sat/vB conditions.
evidence: Part of issue #32093 tracking migration of RPC fee rates to sat/vB units.

Author notes in PR description: "Returning feerates in BTC/kvB it can be very burdensome and is not good practice, as the most widely adopted units are sat/vB." and "Because of sub 1sat/vB environment we cannot rely on GetFee() because it internally uses FeeFrac EvaluateFee() function which rounds the values to always return an int."
result.changed_since_previous: Added top-level named argument support for options across the modified RPC methods, updated `vRPCConvertParams` in `rpc/client.cpp`, and added functional tests for named parameter conversion in `test/functional/rpc_named_arguments.py`.
result.card: This pull request adds an optional sat_vb boolean option to getmempoolinfo, getnetworkinfo, estimatesmartfee, and estimaterawfee, enabling callers to receive feerates in sat/vB rather than legacy BTC/kvB. It addresses developer friction and potential rounding errors from client-side unit conversions, particularly in sub-1 sat/vB environments. Formatting is handled via a new ValueFromFeeRate helper providing 3 decimal places of precision for sat/vB output, and options are made accessible via named RPC arguments. Part of issue #32093, this change has no dependencies.

risk.why: A mistake in feerate formatting or unit conversion could cause downstream wallets and scripts to miscalculate transaction fees.
